summary: Generate 7 publication-grade matplotlib figures for the OpenQG IEEE paper

result.description: Double-column (7.16x3.4 in) left-to-right architecture diagram of the OpenQG V7 engine in four labeled bands: PROPOSAL (jnoccio-fusion router over 131 models/16 providers feeding a best-of-K=4 RouterProposer with 4 lane chips and a parse+oracle-repair self-loop), the emphasized ORACLE core (sketch expander -> truth binding -> physics_kills cascade -> ScorecardV4 with the 100-pt rubric split -> evidence term), EVOLUTION (island population, re-clothe operator, promotable-gated cross-run memory, with a green "next slot" return arrow to the proposer), and AUDIT (streaming ledgers fed by a dashed write bus, replay with 0 mismatches, 21-agent + 12-review adversarial audits). A thick vermillion feedback arrow runs from the audits back into the oracle band labeled "each exploit -> permanent regression test". PNG preview at /home/ubuntu/openQG/paper/figs/fig1_architecture.png; script at /tmp/fig_fig1_architecture.py. Automated checks reported 0 text overflows and 0 pairwise text overlaps.
result.caveats: Pure schematic; no numeric data plotted. Box wording follows the spec verbatim except for line-wrapping ("physics_kills" title split onto two lines, scorecard rubric wrapped to three lines, ledger sublabel wrapped) and ASCII arrows rendered as Unicode arrows. The "everything -> ledgers" requirement is represented by a dashed bus tapping the ORACLE (evidence box) and EVOLUTION (memory box) bands rather than literally every box, to avoid line crossings. Counts in the diagram (131 models, 21-agent, 12-review, 0 mismatches) are taken from the spec and are consistent with but not re-derived from paper/data/story.json.

result.description: Double-column (7.16x2.9) horizontal timeline of the ZYAL V4->V7 arc: 10 event slots (06-08 to 06-11d) on a central spine with alternating-height stems and short labels, full event labels rotated 28 deg under the axis, and t-values as minor text under the spine. Overlaid on a right 0-100 axis is the champion-score cascade in #D55E00 (87.5 -> 55 -> 77 -> 25 -> 43), each peak annotated in italics with its killer audit (V4.1 rubric-gaming, V6 adjudication+drift, V6.1 lA-bias+novelty-laundering, V7 term registry); the final 43 is starred as the only standing honest score. Three tinted background spans (alpha 0.06, palette blue/green/purple) mark the live V5/V6/V7 campaigns, each labeled "live campaign 6x300 gens". PNG preview at dpi=200: /home/ubuntu/openQG/paper/figs/fig2_timeline.png. Script: /tmp/fig_fig2_timeline.py.
result.caveats: (1) story.json does not link cascade eras to timeline slots, so the mapping was inferred from the labels: V4->slot 0, V5->slot 3 (V5 campaign), V6->slot 6 (V6 campaign), "V6.1 survivor"->slot 7 (21-agent audit), V7->slot 9 (V7 campaign). (2) The right axis ylim secretly extends below 0 (spine/ticks bounded to 0-100) so the score band floats above the timeline stems. (3) Font sizes were bumped above the original 6pt spec by an intentional external edit to the script (base 9pt, killed-by annotations 7pt italic, span labels 7.5pt); kept as modified. (4) "lA" from the data is rendered as a Unicode script-l (lA = acoustic scale). (5) The final 43's value label is folded into the "honest 43 - standing" annotation instead of a separate number; "6x300 gens" matches the 6 chunks per campaign in campaigns.json (V5 chunks show ~43-50 logged attempts each, so "300 gens" is taken from the spec/story, not re-derived). Rotated x-tick labels have overlapping axis-aligned bounding boxes by construction, but glyph rows are separated by ~0.29 in (verified geometrically); all other text/line/stem collisions check to zero.

(1) In campaigns.json, V6's first chunk ('v6-chunk-1-partial') has attempts_n=0 (no attempt-level records), so both panels effectively cover V6 chunks 2-6; this is self-consistent since funnels.json v6 totals (626, ok=52) match those same attempts exactly. (2) campaigns.json's 'v7' entry has chunk keys misnamed 'v6-chunk-*' and contains 6 chunk entries, while the spec-mandated label says 'chunks 1-3 + partial'; I used the spec label as instructed. The funnels.json 'v7_partial' counts (724 calls, ok=73) match the campaigns.json v7 attempts exactly, so the data is internally consistent. (3) V5 attempts carry lane=None, so no per-lane breakdown is possible for V5 (spec only asks for V6/V7 there). (4) V5's killed/parse_error/llm_error segments (1/2/3 calls) are sliver-thin and effectively invisible at column width. Sanity asserts in the script confirm per-lane ok sums equal funnel ok counts.
result.description: Two stacked panels (3.5x3.6 in, IEEE single column). TOP: horizontal stacked outcome funnels for V5 (n=276, ok=46), V6 (n=626, ok=52), and V7 chunks 1-3 + partial (n=724, ok=73), segments ok/killed/parse_error/llm_error/empty_output/engine_error in the colorblind-safe palette, with a thin-arrow annotation showing V5's empty_output plague (213 calls) vanishing in V6/V7 while killed comes to dominate as the oracle sharpens. BOTTOM: grouped vertical bars of per-lane OK yields, V6 vs V7, value-labeled — planck_mu0 18->31, dark_scattering 5->9, free 10->13, null_diagnostic 19->20, showing V7's yield gain concentrated in the planck_mu0 lane. PNG preview at dpi=200 saved alongside; script at /tmp/fig_fig3_funnels.py.

Double-column (7.16x3.0) three-panel activity raster from paper/data/campaigns.json: per-chunk rows vs generation (1-300) showing attempt events (gray '|' = killed by oracle, green dot = ok, vermillion 'x' = parse/LLM/other error), with non-DQ scored proposals overlaid as viridis-colored circles (vmin=0, vmax=80, single shared colorbar labeled "proposal score /100") and each chunk's champion total in 6pt bold at the row's right edge. Panels: V5 (6 chunks, 37 proposals, flat ~33.7 scores, champions 55), V6 (6 chunks, 140 proposals, scores up to 77), V7 first 3 chunks only (champions 43/43/25). The progression shows proposal density and score spread rising era over era while the oracle's kill rate dominates V6/V7. PNG preview at /home/ubuntu/openQG/paper/figs/fig4_activity.png (dpi=200).
result.caveats: 1) The spec's "parse/llm errors" 'x' category was broadened to include empty_output (213, nearly all in V5) and engine_error (11) so no events are silently dropped; legend says "parse/LLM/other error". 2) V5 has almost no oracle kills in the data (1 of 1496 events) — the "oracle keeps killing" pattern only appears from V6 on; V5's failures are mostly empty_output. 3) v6-chunk-1-partial has zero attempts/proposals, so V6 row 1 is empty except its champion score (60). 4) V5 champion totals (55) exceed every V5 proposal score (max 33.7) — champion totals evidently come from a later/different scoring pass; plotted as-is. 5) Spec gave two V7 labels ("first 3 chunks" vs panel title "V7 (partial)"); the title list won, and "first 3 chunks shown" was added as a small in-panel note. 6) DQ'd proposals (dq==true) are not overlaid, per spec.

result.description: Four-bar resolution of the h-Omega_m degeneracy valley from paper/data/story.json "valley": V5 diagonal (+54.9) and V6 covariance (+68.8) in orange show the same parameter drift apparently favored by tens of nats, while V6.1 diag calibrated+Occam (-20.5) and V6.1 covariance (-31.9) in blue show it disfavored once accounting is honest. Annotations explain the mechanism: the engine's ell_A bias of +0.755 (8.4 sigma, ~35 nats of spurious evidence, computed from la_bias raw-published over sigma) inflated the V5/V6 bars, and the V6->V6.1 transition (anchor calibration + Occam 0.5 k ln n penalty, curved arrow) flips the sign. Bottom note records that the identical drift direction (h=0.718, Om=0.282, w0=-1.14) is evaluated under each successive rubric, so the "open valley" was a model-error artifact, not physics. PNG preview at /home/ubuntu/openQG/paper/figs/fig5_valley.png (dpi=200); script at /tmp/fig_fig5_valley.py.
result.caveats: The "~35 nats of model error" figure is 0.5*(bias/sigma)^2 = 35.1 nats derived from story.json la_bias (0.7546/0.090 = 8.38 sigma), an inferred Gaussian log-evidence contribution -- it matches the spec's claim but is not stored explicitly in the data. story.json gives v5_diag=54.87 and v61_diag=-20.48, displayed as +54.9/-20.5 per spec rounding. The bottom-note parameter values (h=0.718, Om=0.282, w0=-1.14) come only from the spec text; they do not appear in any file under paper/data/. Y-axis label and annotations use mathtext (Delta ln Z, ell_A, Omega_m) rather than the spec's plain-ASCII strings.

result.description: Double-column two-panel figure (7.16x3.2, gridspec 5:2). LEFT: pulls (data-model)/sigma for the 17 admitted observables (H0, S8, five fsigma8 bins, seven BAO distance ratios, three CMB compressed parameters) for Planck LCDM (filled blue circles + thin line), mu0=-0.1 certified (open green squares), and dark scattering A=2, w0=-0.9 (open orange triangles), with +-1 sigma shaded band, +-2 sigma dashed lines, and the H0 point annotated at +5.4 sigma. RIGHT: growth-sector zoom, fsigma8(z) data with error bars at z=0.067-1.48 against the three model curves, showing the growth data sitting low and the suppressed-growth models (mu0, dark scattering) bending toward them. PNG preview at /home/ubuntu/openQG/paper/figs/fig6_data.png (dpi=200).
result.caveats: (1) Six observables in observables.jsonl have no entry in predictions.txt and are excluded from the pulls panel: dm/dh_over_rd@0.706, dm/dh_over_rd@1.317, dv_over_rd@1.491, and bbn_yp. (2) The dark-scattering model's cmb_lA pull is +30.7 sigma, far off scale; its marker is clipped at the top axis edge (y=6.3) and annotated "+30.7 sigma" with an arrow — the plotted position is not its true value. Its cmb_R pull (+3.5 sigma) is plotted at true value. (3) lcdm and mu0 predictions are identical for everything except fsigma8 (and their cmb_R/cmb_lA pulls are exactly 0, i.e. predictions match data to the quoted digits), so blue and green markers coincide at most x positions; a small horizontal dodge (+-0.16) keeps all three models visible. (4) Model "curves" in the right panel are straight-line connections through only the five prediction points (notably a long segment from z=0.61 to z=1.48), not continuous theory curves.

result.description: Horizontal stacked bars decompose five scorecards into six rubric components (derivation rigor, data fit, novel prediction, unification, robustness-under-judge, parsimony), ordered top-to-bottom V5 champion (55) -> V6 champion (77) -> V6.1 nDGP survivor (60, hatched with skull-note "DQ under V7: no brane term") -> V7 champion planck-mu0-suppressed-0.1 (43) -> human GR+LCDM baseline (80, alpha 0.55, "(V4-era rubric, indicative)"). In-segment values and bold bar-end totals show where each era's points came from: V5/V6 leaned on data_fit+novelty later exposed as artifacts, the survivor leaned on derivation rigor that the V7 term registry disqualified, while V7's 43 points contain no data_fit and are all re-earnable under the strictest gate. PNG preview at /home/ubuntu/openQG/paper/figs/fig7_scorecards.png (dpi=200); both files verified non-empty.
result.caveats: V5 (55) and V6 (77) components read directly from paper/data/story.json (v5_champ_components, v6_77_components; totals verified). V7 (43), V6.1 survivor (60), and human baseline (80) components are hardcoded per spec, not present in any data file; the spec itself calls V7 "approximating 43" (components sum exactly to 43) and flags the human baseline as V4-era-rubric indicative only. Note story.json's cascade lists the V6.1 survivor era champion at 25.0, not 60 — the spec's 60 (pre-DQ survivor scorecard) was used as instructed. Legend label shortened to "Robustness (judge)" to fit single-column width; tight-cropped PDF is 3.54 in wide (0.04 in over nominal 3.5 in column due to bbox_inches='tight'). Script at /tmp/fig_fig7_scorecards.py.
